scope: Five original B310 selectors across seven transport modes: credential legacy/signed, trigger, GitHub review, engine registration, provenance legacy/signed.

selectors.rationale: Authenticated requests now use HTTP(S)-only initial URLs and same-origin-only redirects. A foreign scheme, hostname, effective port or URL userinfo is refused before the redirected request; existing authority-mode no-redirect behavior remains stricter.
selectors.validation: tests/test_authenticated_redirects.py exercises real two-server HTTP redirects using synthetic credentials; all 301/302/303/307/308 GET redirects and POST 302 redirects refuse foreign origins.

before: Seven HTTP 302 reproduction cases failed before the affected clients adopted the helper: four initial client modes and three registration/provenance modes. A second local origin received synthetic credential-bearing requests; no real credentials or external endpoints were used.
after: 388 focused tests passed, including 52 new redirect/scheme boundary cases and existing credential, trigger/control, review, registration/amendment and provenance behavior.
compatibility: Same-origin redirects and legacy internal HTTP remain supported. SigV4 still signs the initial request as before; authority-mode credential requests retain the existing refusal of all redirects.
packaging: Dockerfile already copies the whole worker lib directory and each client package. No new dependency. Worker image rebuild/rollout remains with #6111.
remaining_scope: This is a bounded source fix and does not complete #6108 or reclassify its other observations.
